Subject: Short-lived SAN certs vs wildcard for private endpoints — proposal + ops implications

Team,

Attached is a short proposal (PDF) outlining an internal ACME gateway approach to issue short-lived SAN certificates for customer private endpoints in our Private deployment product. TL;DR: instead of one wildcard cert per customer domain we propose issuing per-endpoint SAN certs (30 day TTL) signed by our internal CA and automating the lifecycle via an internal ACME service behind the VPC control plane.

Why we're looking at this:
- Security: reduces blast radius of leaked keys; easier revocation targeting.
- Multi-tenant naming: customers using split-horizon DNS often have overlapping hostnames across environments; SAN issuance lets us be explicit per FQDN.
- Compliance: customers with strict cert rotation windows want shorter-lived certs and auditability.

Operational trade-offs and questions in the doc:
- DNS provenance: how we verify ACME challenge for private domains (DNS01 + split-horizon or internal challenge proxy).
- DNS ownership model: who controls the zones and TTLs; required CNAME delegation suggestions.
- Key management: internal CA HSM integration, cert archival, and CRL/OCSP strategy.
- Fallback: what happens when ACME gateway is unavailable (short-term accept cached certs + alerting).

Please review: "split-horizon-dns-acme-flow.png" and the ops checklist. Looking for a go/no-go on piloting this with Nebula Health (they asked for short-lived certs and tighter audit trails).

Next steps I propose:
1) Ops + SRE review (karthik, hiro) for automation and availability constraints
2) Legal/Security review for CA trust model and customer-facing docs (marissa can coordinate)
3) Pilot agreement with Nebula (we can offer a temporary dedicated keying approach)

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few quick notes from the enterprise/SE side: 

- Nebula Health is explicitly asking for certificate rotation every 30 days and wants proof-of-rotation in the audit bundle. They have a central security team that will require OCSP stapling logs (or equivalent) and an immutable store of rotation events.

- Marketing note: if we advertise "short-lived certs for private domains" we should include an optional add-on for ASR (audit support + extended retention).

Thanks — read the proposal and the ops checklist. A few technical clarifications and concerns from SRE/infra: 

1) DNS01 in split-horizon: we can't reach external authoritative DNS for many customers in air-gapped setups. Two options: a) delegated private subzone (customer creates delegation to _redwood.<zone>) that we can write TXT records to via a cross-account secure webhook, or b) an internal ACME challenge proxy that the customer's infra runs (sidecar) to respond to challenges locally. Both have trade-offs — option (a) centralizes control (better for us) but requires customer-side DNS changes and support; option (b) demands a small footprint sidecar we need to maintain across distros.

2) Rate limiting and mass issuance: issuing thousands of short-lived certs requires batching and backoff to avoid hammering our internal CA and HSM. We need a token-bucket issuance queue and an overflow policy (issue from a pre-generated short-lived pool + rotate on replenish).

3) CRL vs OCSP: OCSP stapling preferred. But customers in private deployments may not allow outbound OCSP traffic. We should support OCSP responder behind the private network or provide signed stapled OCSP responses at issuance time for a short validity window.

4) Rollback/fallback: propose a two-tier cache: primary (automated) rotating cert and secondary (manual) long-lived cert pinned by customer for emergency only. That must be explicit in the SLA.

I'll sketch a minimal viable implementation and call out operational runbooks (failure modes, HSM failover, audit trail push to customer's S3-compatible store). See attached ops-checklist.

-Karthik

All — quick update after internal infra sync this morning. We're comfortable moving forward with a guarded pilot under these constraints: 

- Pilot scope: Nebula Health only, up to 25 private endpoints across their staging and prod VPCs. We'll opt for delegated private subzone approach (DNS delegation to _redwood.nebula.internal) for initial simplicity.
- Issuance policy: 30-day cert TTL, automatic renewal at day 25; OCSP stapling responses will be generated and stored in the customer's private object store for audit retrieval.
- Failure handling: if ACME gateway fails, we will serve cached certs with explicit expiration warnings in the console and 1hr grace period for token rotation; incident response will be on-call infra + SE.
- Security: internal CA keys will live in our HSM cluster with dual-region replication; access requires approval via the internal PKI change workflow.
- Next steps: Jonas to draft the pilot SoW for Nebula; Marissa to coordinate customer acceptance criteria and legal; Karthik to produce a runbook and a small PoC sidecar for challenge delegation.

Alice (Nebula) — are you OK with the delegated private subzone approach? If so we'll send the delegation CNAME instructions and a timeline.

Thanks,
